question.problem: Consider the function $f(x,y)=2\sqrt{xy}.$ What is the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(8,2)$ in the direction in which the function decreases most rapidly?
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ decreases most rapidly in the opposite direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $-∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(8,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}-∇f(x,y) & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\sqrt{xy})i-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{xy})j \\  & =-\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}\,i-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\,j \\ -∇f(8,2) & =-\sqrt{\frac{2}{8}}\,i-\sqrt{\frac{8}{2}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,i-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(8,2)$ in the direction of $-∇f(8,2)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖-∇f(8,2)‖ & =‖-\frac{1}{2}\,i-2\,j‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{17}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
